# Sources

- [[wiki/sources/2d-graph-js-rendering-tools|2D knowledge graph libraries: an executive summary]] — Five JavaScript graph-rendering libraries compared on scale, execution model and looks, with Sigma.js the pragmatic pick and Cosmograph the only one that survives 100k+ nodes.
- [[wiki/sources/agent-reasoning-memory-why-it-matters-and-how-to-use-it|Agent Reasoning Memory — why it matters and how to use it]] — A study of Neo4j's agent-memory work arguing for a third memory type — traces of how problems were solved — alongside short-term and long-term memory.
- [[wiki/sources/agentic-graphrag-via-mcp-servers|Agentic GraphRAG via MCP Servers]] — An end-to-end technical report on a digital-twin memory — ETL into MongoDB, LLM graph extraction, hybrid retrieval, and a six-tool FastMCP server that any harness can drive.
- [[wiki/sources/article-building-a-coding-agent-from-scratch-system-design|Building a Coding Agent From Scratch]] — The system design of a coding-agent harness — one headless core with six modules around the loop, two interfaces over one message bus, and an evals layer on top.
- [[wiki/sources/article-context-engineering-for-coding-agents|Context Engineering for Coding Agents]] — The four harness components that keep a context window high-signal — memory, skills, an LSP server and compaction — with the thresholds each one fires at.
- [[wiki/sources/article-the-coding-agent-loop|The Bare-Bones Coding Agent Loop]] — The implementation lesson — one agent loop, nine tools, three input modes (steer, follow-up, abort), and the session log that makes a turn replayable.
- [[wiki/sources/building-graphrag-from-scratch-infrastructure-over|Building GraphRAG from scratch: infrastructure over frameworks]] — A two-day from-scratch GraphRAG build, and the argument behind it — infrastructure tools solve the hard problems, AI frameworks abstract the easy ones and fight your data model.
- [[wiki/sources/choosing-an-inference-architecture-for-your-agents|Choosing an Inference Architecture for Your Agents]] — One question decides how you pay for inference — is a human waiting? — yielding three architectures: interactive, remote, and async offload.
- [[wiki/sources/constraints|Constraints]] — Three lines of page-count constraints for a book — a scope note, not a technical one.
- [[wiki/sources/deep-dive-on-how-to-scale-your-graphrag-ingestion-pipeline|Scaling a GraphRAG pipeline from 1 machine to 100 — the worker-queue pattern]] — Prefect's server / work pool / worker split, the staged path from serve() to Kubernetes, and the four independent concurrency controls that keep it from overrunning an API.
- [[wiki/sources/designing-an-agents-memory-in-a-nutshell|Designing an agent's memory in a nutshell]] — A two-line pointer note flagging Neo4j's agent-memory series as the reference for memory types, with a matching LinkedIn post.
- [[wiki/sources/different-levels-of-hosting-your-embedding-models|Different Levels of Hosting Your Embedding Models]] — A four-tier guide to running embedding models — mocked in tests, Sentence Transformers in dev, vLLM on serverless GPUs in prod — held together by one interface.
- [[wiki/sources/e2e-personal-assistant-architecture-using-mongodb-as-a|e2e personal assistant architecture using MongoDB as a unified memory]] — A pointer note holding a video walkthrough and its transcript for the end-to-end personal-assistant architecture built on MongoDB.
- [[wiki/sources/explaining-the-architecture|Explaining the Architecture]] — A brainstorm-style walkthrough of a second-brain agent — GraphRAG ingestion, an agentic retrieval layer with three memory types, and FastMCP as the serving surface.
- [[wiki/sources/feedback-from-v1|Feedback from V1]] — Four reader-feedback pointers for a book's second edition — more theory up front, open-source best practices, agentic AI, a stronger evaluation chapter.
- [[wiki/sources/four-prefect-task-runners-four-different-problems|I tested all 4 Prefect task runners — the decision tree I wish existed]] — Async I/O, sync blocking I/O, CPU-bound and GPU-bound work need four mechanically different concurrency tools; most API-driven pipelines need none of them.
- [[wiki/sources/graphrag-presentation|GraphRAG presentation — Context Engineering with GraphRAG, building your digital twin]] — A 17-slide deck with worked examples — three extraction strategies on one email, bottom-up vs top-down retrieval, and the cat-vet query that stitches four silos.
- [[wiki/sources/high-level-graphrag-architecture-built-on-top-of-mcp-servers|High-Level GraphRAG Architecture Built on Top of MCP Servers]] — A lecture write-up covering the whole arc — context rot and data fragmentation, ontologies, immutable logs, materialization, bottom-up and top-down retrieval, and agentic GraphRAG.
- [[wiki/sources/how-smooth-is-to-use-prefect-for-agentic-coding|Prefect is the only orchestrator that survives agentic coding]] — Why an orchestrator's fitness for AI-assisted development is decided by one question — can the agent restart the execution environment in seconds after a code change?
- [[wiki/sources/how-smooth-was-my-experience-to-use-mongodb-and-build-from|One database, three search modes — a full GraphRAG layer on MongoDB in 2 days]] — The implementation-level account of running text, vector and graph search on a local MongoDB, including the four gotchas that cost real time.
- [[wiki/sources/how-to-ingest-1-000-000-documents-into-your-agent-memory|How to Ingest 1,000,000 Documents Into Your Agent Memory]] — A pointer note for a two-part walkthrough on scaling a GraphRAG ingestion pipeline to ~1M documents from HuggingFace, RSS, YouTube and crawled sites.
- [[wiki/sources/how-to-integrate-skills-into-mcp-servers-mcp-prompts-vs|How to integrate Skills into MCP servers: MCP Prompts vs. Skills]] — Working notes establishing that skills are not an MCP primitive, and that FastMCP's skills provider leaves them in a dead zone where clients can list them but never invoke them agentically.
- [[wiki/sources/how-to-structure-your-collections-as-immutable-logs-instead|Structuring collections as immutable logs instead of one-shot collections]] — Why the ontology is the most important step in GraphRAG, and how append-only observation logs plus a materialized view fix the deduplication and provenance that embedded arrays make impossible.
- [[wiki/sources/how-you-pay-for-llm-inference|How You Pay for LLM Inference]] — The overlooked cost dimension — per-token versus GPU-hour, and serverless versus reserved — worked through with napkin math on a 1,000-document job.

- [[wiki/sources/marketing|Marketing]] — Positioning notes for a book's second edition — sell the topic changes rather than the chapter count.
- [[wiki/sources/mcp-servers-for-continual-learning-via-graphrag|MCP Servers for Continual Learning via GraphRAG]] — A deep dive on tool design for an agentic GraphRAG memory — six tools, why not one, and the deliberate asymmetry of orchestrating writes but never reads.
- [[wiki/sources/modeling-knowledge-graph-collections-append-only-log-vs-one|Modeling knowledge graph collections: append-only log vs. one collection]] — The full engineering account of the two-collection design — and the note that records its abandonment in favour of a single mutable collection with in-place upserts.
- [[wiki/sources/mongodb-for-an-ai-agent-unified-memory|MongoDB for an AI Agent Unified Memory]] — An evaluation of MongoDB as the single store behind agent memory — documents, vectors, bounded graph traversal and an append-only event log — with the thresholds at which specialized databases win.
- [[wiki/sources/mongodb-notes-on-scaling-from-the-meeting|MongoDB Notes on Scaling (from the meeting)]] — Raw meeting notes from a scaling review — questions about an append-only log plus materialized graph, and answers about shards, replicas, RAM and the $merge sync.
- [[wiki/sources/normalization-entity-resolution|Normalization / Entity Resolution]] — A one-line plan for a deep dive into entity resolution during knowledge-graph extraction, made durable with Prefect, referencing Neo4j's resolution guide.
- [[wiki/sources/owning-your-context-layer|Owning Your Context Layer]] — A post arguing that models and harnesses are commoditized, so the only remaining moat is a memory you own and can carry between harnesses through an MCP server.

- [[wiki/sources/questions-and-remarks-from-people-while-posting|Questions And Remarks From People While Posting]] — Reader questions collected from posts — memory decay, wrong extractions, freshness at scale, ontology construction — plus one practitioner's GraphRAG success report.
- [[wiki/sources/questions-around-embeddings-with-mongodb-voyage-ai|Questions Around Embeddings with MongoDB & Voyage AI]] — A Q&A with the vendor on where embeddings should be computed — Hugging Face locally, the Voyage or Atlas API in production, auto-embedding for enterprise.
- [[wiki/sources/rdf-vs-labeled-property-graphs|RDF vs. Labeled Property Graphs]] — Why property graphs beat RDF triples in practice, and the three extraction modes — structured, semi-structured, unstructured — that decide whether a graph is production-ready.
- [[wiki/sources/retrieval-strategies|Retrieval strategies for GraphRAG: graph search, deep search, agentic search]] — The three ways an agent searches its unified memory, the multi-hop traversal that makes it GraphRAG, and the design rule underneath — orchestrate the writes, never the reads.
- [[wiki/sources/rrf-fusion-hybrid-search-without-reranker|You don't need a reranker for hybrid search — RRF fusion in 20 lines]] — Why Reciprocal Rank Fusion replaces a cross-encoder reranker for hybrid retrieval — rank arithmetic instead of score comparison, with the implementation and its limits.
- [[wiki/sources/running-multiple-graphrag-ingestion-pipelines-in-parallel|Two dimensions of parallelism — pipelines in parallel vs. tasks in parallel]] — Flow-level and task-level parallelism are independent axes that multiply, and most pipelines only use one — worked through to a million-document ingestion plan.
- [[wiki/sources/scaling-graphrag-ingestion-pipelines-with-prefect|Scaling GraphRAG Ingestion Pipelines with Prefect]] — A ghostwriter brief pricing the three expensive ingestion steps — extraction, resolution, embedding — and showing how checkpointing plus a worker-queue pattern stops you paying twice.
- [[wiki/sources/scaling-mongodb-brain-dump|Scaling MongoDB Brain Dump]] — A worked narrative of database scaling for agent memory — replicas, sharding, and the argument that RAM, not data size, is what actually constrains a knowledge graph.
- [[wiki/sources/stop-using-mcp-servers-to-access-your-mongodb-postgres|Stop using MCP Servers to access your MongoDB/Postgres database when using coding agents]] — A short argument that database access for coding agents is one line in CLAUDE.md pointing at mongosh or psql, not an MCP server — and where that stops being true.
- [[wiki/sources/system-architecture-of-future-ai-apps-ui-tui-ide-extension|System architecture of future AI apps — presentation, harness, connectivity, MCP servers]] — A four-layer architecture breakdown of where AI apps are converging, with the harness-side patterns (progressive discovery, code mode) that make the rest work.
- [[wiki/sources/the-future-of-mcp-vs-skills|The Future of MCP vs. Skills]] — Talk notes from an MCP maintainer arguing that connectivity is a stack — skills, CLIs and MCP each for their own job — and laying out the 2026 protocol roadmap.
- [[wiki/sources/the-future-of-mcp-why-the-future-of-agents-is-mcp-skills|The future of MCP — why the future of agents is MCP, skills and CLIs combined]] — A short LinkedIn post draft laying out a four-layer architecture for AI-native applications — presentation, harness plus runtime, connectivity, MCP servers.
- [[wiki/sources/the-right-way-of-building-agents-with-mcp-servers|The Right Way of Building Agents With MCP Servers]] — A walkthrough of a GraphRAG-backed personal-assistant architecture that ends in an open architectural question — should the custom orchestrator live on the MCP server or in the client?
- [[wiki/sources/tivadar-danka-knowledge-graph-questions|Tivadar Danka Knowledge Graph Questions]] — Someone else's minimal knowledge graph — 810 ML algorithms in a JSON file, recursively expanded by an LLM, categorized, unnormalized, rendered with Three.js.
- [[wiki/sources/walkthrough-throw-the-ingestion-and-retrieval-logic|Walkthrough through the ingestion and retrieval logic]] — A compact end-to-end description of the memory pipeline, including the decision to embed document summaries instead of chunks and to let embedding clusters replace topic entities.
- [[wiki/sources/what-to-focus-on|What to Focus On]] — A short priority note — build the ingestion path next, to unblock the extraction model and to stress-test MongoDB and Prefect in public.
